title: Protocol for multimodal analysis of human kidney tissue by imaging mass spectrometry and CODEX multiplexed immunofluorescence
protocol: Prepare the kidney tissue for freezing.
Cut the kidney in half coronally, generally along its longest plane.
Cut out a portion of the kidney (∼80 × 60 × 4 mm) that is farthest away from tumor or diseased areas using a scalpel or other blade.
Photograph the smaller piece of kidney in reference to its original location within the entire kidney.
Further cut the piece of kidney into 3–5 smaller pieces (∼2 × 15 × 4 mm).
Photograph the smaller pieces to reference how they were cut.
Place a layer of dry ice into a freezer box and add enough isopentane to make a slurry.
Remove kidney tissue blocks from plastic encasing and measure the weight, length, width, and height.
Place a metal weigh boat on top of the isopentane slurry and let cool.
Write the sample number and orientation onto mold edges, indicating inner/outer and superior/inferior edges.
Add tissue to the metal boat and wait until the tissue is completely frozen.
Add enough 2.6% carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) to cover the bottom of the embedding mold.
Place the embedding mold with CMC on top of the isopentane slurry.
Wait until CMC starts to freeze and begins to turn opaque.
Place tissue onto a freezing CMC layer.
Slowly add more CMC until the tissue is completely covered.
Wrap the frozen tissue in foil.
Label the wrapped tissue.
Store the labeled and wrapped tissue at -80°C.
Place a non-frozen piece of tissue into an embedding cassette with the cut side facing down.
Submerge the tissue in a 10% neutral-buffered formalin solution for at least 12 hours but typically 18 hours.
Move the tissue cassettes into 70% ethanol for 35 minutes.
Submerge the tissue in 90% ethanol for 35 minutes.
Submerge the tissue in 95% ethanol for 35 minutes.
Submerge the tissue in three sequential containers of 100% ethanol, each for 35 minutes.
Submerge the tissue in 100% xylenes for 35 minutes, repeated three times (total of 105 minutes).
Fresh xylene solutions are required for each separate submersion.
Submerge the tissue in paraffin (wax) for 60 minutes, repeated three times (total of 3 hours).
Embed the tissue with additional paraffin at approximately 20°C to make a block such that the tissue is entirely encased.
Deparaffinize tissue by submerging in xylenes for 3 min, twice.
Submerge the tissue in 100% ethanol for 1 min, twice.
Submerge the tissue in 95% ethanol for 1 min.
Submerge the tissue in 70% ethanol for 1 min.
Submerge the tissue in 100% water for 1 min.
Rinse tissues with generous amounts of distilled water.
Incubate the tissue in 0.5% periodic acid in distilled water for 10 min.
Rinse the tissues generously with distilled water.
Incubate the tissues in Schiff’s reagent for 30 min.
Rinse tissues in warm (∼40°C) water.
Counterstain the tissue in hematoxylin for 1 min.
Rinse the tissue generously with distilled water.
Dip the tissue section into 0.5% ammonium hydroxide once and rinse with generous amounts of distilled water until runoff water is colorless.
Dehydrate the tissue using graded alcohol solutions, dipping ten times each in 95%, 95%, 100%, and 100% ethanol sequentially.
Submerge the tissue in xylenes for 1 min twice.
Coverslip the tissues by adding 2-3 drops of cytoseal to the tissue surface after submerging in xylenes, then slowly placing the coverslip on the slide.
Set the internal temperature of the cryostat to −21°C and object temperature to −20°C.
Clean the blade with ethanol and a lint free wipe before placing the blade into the cryostat.
Mount CMC embedded tissue onto a cold chuck using OCT, ensuring OCT does not touch the tissue directly.
Shave a flat surface onto the mounting surface using a razor blade for correct orientation.
Adjust the angle of the sectioning stage for quality sectioning.
Trim the CMC shell using increments of 30–50 μm until tissue becomes visible.
Remove excess CMC surrounding the tissue with a cooled razor blade.
Set the section thickness setting to 10 μm and section until the portion of the tissue for multimodal analysis is reached.
Position the anti-roll bar ahead of the blade, ensuring it does not scrape the tissue.
Section tissue until the desired number of sections are acquired.
Manipulate sections onto slides using a fine-tipped paint brush and thaw mount using a gloved hand.
Place mounted, cut tissue on a 20°C hot plate for 30 seconds.
Mount tissue sections onto indium tin oxide coated slides for imaging mass spectrometry analysis.
Mount tissue sections onto poly-lysine coated coverslips for CODEX immunofluorescence analysis.
Store tissue sections in a desiccator if undergoing immediate analysis within 24 hours or store them at -80°C within a vacuum-sealed slide holder for longer term storage.
Perform autofluorescence microscopy on each tissue section to acquire a nondestructive image of the tissue for later registration.
Place the slide within the microscope adapter and insert into the Zeiss AxioScan Slide Scanner or equivalent.
Perform coarse focusing on the tissue using the DAPI filter set.
Use lamp power of 90% and exposure times of 150 ms.
Perform fine focusing on the tissue using the DAPI, GFP, and DsRed filter sets.
Build a focus map using lamp power of 90% and exposure times of 150 ms.
Define an imaging region that includes the entire tissue section.
Acquire an autofluorescence image.
Submerge the tissue section into 750 μL of TRIzoILS.
Homogenize the sample by passing through a 23G syringe needle.
Passage the homogenized sample through a 27G syringe needle.
Freeze the homogenate solution on dry ice.
Thaw the frozen homogenate and mix by vortexing.
Dilute the homogenate solution with RNase free water to a final volume of 960 μL.
Add 40 μL of a 5 mg/mL glycogen solution to the homogenate.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Incubate for 5 min at 20°C.
Add 250 μL of chloroform to the mixture.
Vortex the mixture for 15 seconds.
Centrifuge the mixture at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Pipette the supernatant into a new container.
Add 600 μL of isopropanol to the supernatant and mix well.
Incubate the mixture at -20°C for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 20,000 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 600 μL of 80% ethanol diluted in RNase-free water to the mixture and vortex.
Centrifuge the solution at 20,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Dry down the sample using nitrogen or another inert gas.
Add 300 μL of RLT plus buffer containing 1% 2-ME to the dried sample and mix well.
Add 450 μL of 100% ethanol to the mixture.
Transfer 750 μL of the solution to a RNeasy MinElute spin column.
Centrifuge the column for 1 minute at 12,000 × g and 24°C.
Centrifuge the phase lock gel at 12,000 × g for 5 minutes before adding the TRIzol mixture.
Add 500 μL of RPE buffer to the column and mix with the TRIzol mixture.
Centrifuge the solution at 12,000 × g for 1 minute at 24°C.
Discard the flow through from the column.
Add an additional 500 μL of RPE buffer to the column and centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 2 minutes at 24°C.
Discard the flow through again.
Centrifuge the mixture again for 1 minute at 12,000 × g and 24°C.
Discard the flow through from this step as well.
Open the column lid and centrifuge it at 12,000 × g for 5 minutes at 24°C to dry the column membrane.
Place the dried column in a new container.
Add 10 μL of RNase-free water to the center of the column membrane.
Incubate the column with the RNase-free water for 2 minutes at 20°C.
Centrifuge the column at 12,000 × g and 24°C for 3 minutes.
Add 10 μL of RNase free water in the center of the column membrane.
Incubate for 2 min at 20°C.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g and 24°C for 3 min.
Obtain the RNA integrity number (RIN) to assess RNA integrity.
Determine the percentage of RNA fragments >200 nucleotides in size (DV 200) to assess RNA integrity.
Apply 6 psi of nitrogen to the sprayer nozzle.
Turn on the TM sprayer and set the nozzle temperature to 40°C.
Change the LC solvent composition to 100% acetonitrile.
Set the flow rate to 0.05 mL/min.
Load the sample loop with 5 mL of pure acetonitrile.
Spray from the sample loop for 2 min to ensure instrument cleanliness.
Load 6 mL of matrix solution (5 mg/mL 1,5-diaminonaphthalene in tetrahydrofuran) into the sample loop.
Switch sprayer to “Inject” and spray for ∼1 min.
Use a blank slide to check that matrix is spraying from the nozzle tip.
Tape slide(s) onto a 75°C heated block on top of stage.
Adjust software scanning area to encompass the entire sample.
Adjust settings in TM Sprayer software to 1350 mm/min nozzle velocity, 1.5 mm track spacing, 0.05 mL/min flow rate, CC Pattern, 2 L/min flow rate, 5 passes, 40 mm nozzle height, and no drying time.
Click “Start” under the “Cycle” tab to initiate coating process.
Click “Continue” to start the matrix coating process.
Inject 20 mL of acetonitrile once the coating process is finished to clean the instrument.
Set the LC flow rate to 1 mL/min for 10 min after injecting acetonitrile.
Clean tip of nozzle with 5 mL of methanol.
Change HLPC flow rate to 0.05 mL/min of 100% acetonitrile.
Shut down the software, turn off the TM Sprayer, and shut the nitrogen off.
Check matrix coating on slide for uniform application.
Scan a 3200-dpi image as a jpg of the matrix coated tissue section held in the MTP-slide adapter II using a flatbed scanner.
Ensure sufficient contrast is present to visualize the tissue boundaries.
Tracing the tissue with a sharpie on the back of the slide may help in visualization and region selection.
Insert the slide adapter plate into the instrument and perform height detection procedures.
Open the FlexImaging software and follow prompts to designate sample file name, method, pitch, scanned image of the slide, etc.
Train the target position with three teaching points.
Create a measurement region around the tissue for IMS analysis.
Go to an area off the tissue and ensure the focus of the laser is adequate for 10 μm spatial resolution imaging.
Start the MS acquisition of the tissue section.
Collect post-IMS autofluorescence microscopy of the MALDI ablated sample.
Perform coarse focusing on the tissue using the GFP filter set (ex. 450–490 nm; em. 500–550, green) with 90% lamp power and 150 ms exposure times.
Perform fine focusing on the tissue using the GFP filter set and brightfield setting.
Define the imaging region that includes the entire tissue.
Acquire brightfield images of the MALDI ablated sample.
Acquire autofluorescence images of the MALDI ablated sample.
Remove matrix by submerging the slide in 100% ethanol for ∼2–3 min or until matrix is gone.
Submerge the slides in 70% ethanol for 3 min.
Perform PAS staining on the tissue section after removing the MALDI matrix.
Conjugate a primary antibody to a unique oligonucleotide barcode.
Add all primary antibodies (<50) to a tissue section at once.
Fix the primary antibodies to the tissue, enhancing tissue integrity.
Serially add and remove secondary (complementary) oligonucleotide barcodes from the tissue.
Block 50 kDa molecular weight cut-off filters with 500 μL of filter blocking solution for 10 minutes at approximately 20°C.
Dilute 50 μg of each antibody into 100 μL in PBS and filter with 50 MW cut-off filters.
Reduce antibodies with the reduction mixture for 25 minutes at approximately 20°C.
Centrifuge the reduced antibodies at 12,000 X g and add buffer solution.
Rehydrate oligonucleotide barcodes in 10 μL nuclease-free water.
Further dilute the rehydrated oligonucleotide barcodes with 210 μL of conjugation solution.
Add respective barcode solutions to the reduced primary antibodies and incubate for 2 hours at approximately 20°C.
Purify the solution by buffer exchanging with purification solution.
Store the purified solution in storage solution at approximately 4°C.
Remove fresh frozen tissue from -80°C and place inside a desiccator for at least 20 min.
Submerge tissues completely in acetone (∼5 mL) for 5 min using a glass petri dish.
Rehydrate tissues in hydration buffer (∼5 mL) for 3 min inside a humidity chamber.
Fix the tissues for 10 min in 1.6% paraformaldehyde in hydration buffer (∼5 mL).
Submerge tissues in excess staining buffer (∼5 mL) for 30 min using a plastic petri dish or other container.
Incubate tissues with a blocking buffer and primary antibody cocktail (1:200 antibody dilution, ∼200 μL) for 3 h within a humidity chamber at ∼20°C.
Rinse samples with staining buffer.
Fix the primary antibodies to the tissue with 1.6% paraformaldehyde in storage buffer for 10 min.
Rinse samples with excess PBS.
Incubate samples in cold methanol for 5 min.
Rinse samples with excess PBS again.
Fix the samples with fixative solution for 10 min before storing them in storage buffer at approximately 4°C.
Perform fluorescence microscopy and CODEX multiplexed immunofluorescence.
Dilute antibodies in reporter solution to a 1:200 dilution with 1 μL of a 1 mg/mL solution of DAPI.
Fill respective bottles with nuclease-free water, 1× CODEX buffer, and dimethyl sulfoxide.
Mount a blank coverslip into the coverslip microfluidic chamber of the CODEX instrument and flush the fluidic lines.
Mount the prepared tissue sample.
Incubate with 1× CODEX buffer and 1 μL of a 1 mg/mL of DAPI for 5 min.
Wash samples with the automated CODEX system.
Set up tiled regions covering the tissue.
Focus at the tissue surface using an automated microscopy setup equipped with a Zeiss Axio and C13440 camera or equivalent equipment.
Convert Bruker (.d) raw file into a custom binary data format in profile mode at native spectral resolution.
Perform mass alignment and calibration of the dataset.
Estimate spectral misalignment for each pixel and correct using PCHIP interpolation or linear shift.
Align spectra based on automatically selected peaks and then recalibrate using well-characterized lipids.
Create a mean mass spectrum by taking the mean of each mass bin in the dataset.
Calculate the ppm error for common lipids, such as [PC(32:0)+H]+ and [PC(34:1)+H]+.
Re-calibrate the entire dataset with additional well-characterized ions if mass error is >3 ppm.
Compute total ion current (TIC)-based normalization factors after alignment and calibration.
Perform peak picking on the mean mass spectrum.
Use the LIPIDMAPS database to annotate each m/z value with a putative annotation.
Specify a narrow 0.005 m/z mass tolerance window.
Select “even chains only”.
Calculate the ppm error associated with each assignment and remove assignments with errors >5 ppm.
Extract peak intensity from the calibrated dataset using one of the available options.
Extract ion images based on an untargeted feature list that has not been narrowed down by the previous step.
Extract ion images based on the identified feature list.
Create narrow 3–5 m/z bin extraction windows for each selected peak.
Generate ion images using the created extraction windows.
Export extracted peak intensities to a columnar CSV file in the format: x, y, m/z 1, m/z 2 … m/z N.
Read-in the table into Python.
Export peak intensities to an imzML file using the pyimzML library.
Align and register each modality using regToolboxMSRC.
Using FIJI ImageJ, select corresponding laser ablation marks in the post-acquisition autofluorescence image map.
Using FIJI ImageJ, select IMS pixels in the IMS pixel map.
Use a "Landmark Correspondences" FIJI plugin to find an affine transformation between the two images.
Select post-AF image as source image within the plugin.
Select IMS pixel map as the template image within the plugin.
Save the transformed and registered post-AF image.
Use wsireg to align other microscopy modalities, such as CODEX multiplexed IF, preIMS AF, PAS or any other associated microscopy image, to the newly saved post-AF image.
Generate pyramidal OME-TIFF images for all images after registration using wsireg.
Scale the IMS data to the same resolution as the microscopy data.
Overlay IMS onto microscopy.
